newsitem.title: USA: Burlington/Santa Fe sees lower Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Burlington/Santa Fe sees lower Q1 earnings.

text.p: Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp expects first quarter earnings to be down about 20 percent from a year earlier due to higher expenses related to continuing problems from winter storms, President and Chief Executive Robert Krebs said Thursday.
Speaking at the company's annual meeting, he said first quarter revenues could be up from a year ago, but earnings will be lower.
"The revenues could be higher, but because of about a three percent increase in expenses, the earnings are expected to be about 20 percent lower in the first quarter," Krebs said.
"And that is the primary reason for the drop in the stock price," he added.
In the 1996 first quarter the company reported earnings of $187 million, or $1.21 per share, on revenues of $2.03 billion.
According to First Call, analysts' consensus first quarter earnings estimate for the company is $0.98 a share.
The company expects to release first quarter earnings next Tuesday.
The company warned of possible lower earnings last month, blaming bad weather and higher expenses related to the weather.
The company's shares were up 3/4 at 72-3/4 in early afternoon trading today, near their 52-week low of 71-1/4. The stock has witnessed a decline since its 52-week high of 90-1/8.

Commenting on 1996 results, the first full year of reporting after the $4 billion merger of Burlington Northern Inc and Santa Fe Pacific Corp, Krebs said the worst snowstorm in U.S. history severly disrupted traffic throughout the Pacific Northwest and the Great Plains.
He said revenues from agricultural commodities freightage was down $120 million last year.
On the plus side, he said, the company undertook capital investment of $2.2 billion to increase capacity and infrastructure improvements.
For the current year, Krebs said weather problems continue to hurt the company. "We have not been off to a good start this year" due to the weather, he said.

Commenting on the integration of Burlington Northern and Santa Fe, he said the company had done well in consolidating the operations of the two companies. "But we have much more to do and we are confident we will do it," he said.
In 1996 the company earned $889 million, or $5.70 per share, on revenues of $8.19 billion.
